author: Ash

copy.intro: You've found the Cold Culture hoodie you want, boxy and cotton, at $109. Then you read the returns: 15 days, and a US return costs €15 or more. If you'd like a longer window, a bigger size or a heavier fleece, these ten brands make the same kind of oversized hoodie, and every one ships to the US. The closest to Cold Culture's price come first.

bodies.blue-banana:
Blue Banana is the closest match on price, and like Cold Culture it's a Madrid label. Its Classic Hoodie (€94.90, about $106) is the one to know: 100% organic cotton with an embroidered X on the chest and back, in ten colors.

It's the one men's hoodie style the brand sells at full price, so it's the fair comparison. The cut is a regular fit, where Cold Culture cuts most of its hoodies boxy, so expect it to sit closer to the body. Sizes run XS to XXL, the same as Cold Culture.

Prices are in euros and US customs is yours to pay, so add both before you compare. What you get back is time: 30 days to return, twice Cold Culture's window, though the postage back is on you. If you'd rather pay in dollars with duties included, try Yuxus.
bodies.yuxus:
Yuxus is the most direct swap: another Madrid brand, with most of its hoodies at $109, right where Cold Culture's sit. Start with the Arctic Belgrave Hoodie ($109), in 450gsm cotton with a washed finish and dropped shoulders.

The weight is the useful part. Most Yuxus listings state 450gsm, while Cold Culture names a weight on only a few of its hoodies, so you know what you're buying before it arrives. To spend less, the Bistre Vanguard Hoodie ($79) is the cheapest at full price.

US orders ship free over $120 with duties and taxes included, a lower bar than Cold Culture's $150. Returns are the same 15 days, and sending one back from the US costs $14.90.
bodies.drmers-club:
DRMERS CLUB is the pick if XXL is where Cold Culture runs out for you. Every full-price hoodie and zip-up comes in XS to XXXL, and most cost $100 or $110, right next to Cold Culture's $109. The Script Text Hoodie ($110) is a good place to start, or the Everything Is Fine Hoodie ($100) if you'd rather spend a little less.

It's a Vancouver label with one store, in Gastown, so for US shoppers it's online only, just like Cold Culture. Shipping is a $7 flat fee and free over $150, the same bar Cold Culture sets.

Read the returns before you buy a drop. You get 14 days and pay the postage back, there are no straight exchanges, and collaboration and limited-edition pieces can't be returned at all.
bodies.mertra:
Mertra is where to go for a heavier, more technical hoodie at close to Cold Culture's price. Most of its hoods cost $118 or $121, and the listings give weights from 460gsm up to 700gsm. The Glide Hood ($121) is 500gsm with hidden zip pockets and hood toggles.

It's an Australian brand, but it keeps warehouses in the US as well as Australia, the UK and the EU. For the cheapest way in, the Pulse Hood ($105) is 460gsm cotton with 3D piping, a detail you won't find on Cold Culture's mostly plain, printed hoodies.

Shipping is worked out at checkout with no free-shipping threshold, so check the total before you pay. Returns are 14 days on full-price pieces, and you start one by email.
bodies.anti-social-social-club:
Anti Social Social Club is the one for team and logo hoodies at Cold Culture money. The Classic Mind Games Hoodie ($89) costs less than Cold Culture's cheapest, and most of the range sits at $119, much of it in NFL team collaborations.

It's a US brand charging in dollars, so there's no conversion or customs to work out. But everything is made to order. Count on 4 to 6 weeks before it ships, then a week or two in transit, so don't order the week before you need it.

The bigger catch is returns. All sales are final, with no exchanges and no store credit, so be sure of your size first. If you want a hoodie at this price that you can send back, DRMERS CLUB gives you 14 days.
bodies.derschutze:
derschutze is the one you can try on in the US: it has a store at 22 Spring Street in New York, as well as London and Berlin. Prices start where Cold Culture's do, with the won Hoodie ($106), and the riot Hoodie ($117) lands right at Cold Culture's top price.

It's a Hamburg brand, and most of its hoodies are 460gsm to 480gsm with embroidered or printed fronts. Its listings say the hoodies fit true to size. That's a different cue from Cold Culture, which tells you to go a size up for the oversized look.

Online, shipping is the catch. A US order costs €23.99 to send with no free threshold, so the New York store is the better deal if you can get there. Returns are 14 days.
bodies.cuotti:
CUOTTI is the cheaper Spanish option, and its whole pitch is weight. Every hoodie is 465gsm cotton with fleece inside, and none costs more than $89. The Sudadera Oversize 465 GSM Negra Logo Bordado ($63) is the cheapest, and the Spanish Luxury hoodies ($74) carry the brand's print across the back.

The range is small, five hoodies at full price, all in black, blue or green, and sizes stop at L. If you wear XL or bigger, skip it and go to DRMERS CLUB.

Returns are open for 14 days, but you get a gift card, not your money back. That's worth knowing before you order a size you're unsure of from Spain.
bodies.corteiz:
Corteiz costs more, but it's close on shape: its hoodies are cut boxy and relaxed, like Cold Culture's, in 430gsm to 440gsm cotton fleece. The Alcatraz Hoodie ($155) is the cheapest way in, and the OG Strike Hoodie ($160) sits in the middle of the range.

It's a UK label that charges US shoppers in dollars, but import duties are yours to pay when the parcel arrives. Cold Culture includes them, so the real gap is wider than the price tags show.

All sales are final, with refunds only for items that arrive damaged. Many of its listings say true to size, so order the size you already wear in other boxy hoodies.
bodies.fear-of-god-essentials:
Fear of God Essentials is the step up in price, from $150 to $195, and its listings give the fleece weight, from 380gsm to 520gsm. The Essentials SS26 Classic Hoodie ($150) is the entry point. The NFL Sport Hoodie ($175) is 480gsm in a relaxed sport fit.

It's sold on Fear of God's own US store, and shipping is free on orders over $100 within the contiguous US. That's the lowest bar here, so a single hoodie clears it. Many styles go up to XXXL, one size past Cold Culture.

The trade-off is returns: every Essentials purchase is final sale, no exceptions. If you want a pricier hoodie you can send back, Represent gives you 14 days.
bodies.represent:
Represent is the British label to look at if you'll pay more for weight and a sharper shape. Its Initial Boxy Hoodie ($140) is the one to compare, in 500gsm brushed-back fleece. It's boxy and cropped short in the body, so it sits wider and higher than a Cold Culture hoodie. Or step up to the Represent Owners Club Hoodie ($200).

From there, prices climb to $315 for embellished and graphic styles, and most of the range states 480gsm or more. Sizes run XS to XXL, with XXS on most styles.

US orders ship from the US, free over $175, and you get 14 days to return. If $140 is already more than you want to spend, Mertra covers the heavy-hoodie side for about $120.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with what you want to spend. Yuxus and Blue Banana sit right at Cold Culture's $109, and CUOTTI comes in under $90 if you wear S to L. DRMERS CLUB and Mertra cost a little more, mostly $100 to $125.

Then check your size. DRMERS CLUB goes to XXXL on every hoodie, and so do many Essentials styles.

If you might send it back, Blue Banana gives you 30 days. Anti Social Social Club, Corteiz and Essentials take nothing back, so buy those in a size you know.

Shipping is the last check. Yuxus includes US duties, just as Cold Culture does, while Corteiz and Blue Banana leave them to you. derschutze charges €23.99 to post a US order, unless you can walk into its New York store.

faqs.a: Yes. It's a Madrid streetwear brand founded in 2021, and its official store is coldcultureworldwide.com. Other sites using the Cold Culture name aren't its store, so check the address before you pay.
In Madrid, where it started in 2021. It also has stores in Barcelona, Valencia, Paris, Milan, London, Berlin and Amsterdam, but none in the US.

faqs.q: Does Cold Culture ship to the US?
faqs.a: Yes. US shipping costs $8.95 and is free on orders over $150. Import duties and taxes are already included, so nothing extra is due when it arrives.
faqs.source_query: does cold culture ship to the us

faqs.q: How long does Cold Culture take to deliver?
faqs.a: To the US, 5 to 10 days by standard shipping. Orders placed after 1:00 PM CET are processed the next business day, and launches, Black Friday and Christmas can add delays.
